facts.statement: Tadzhikosuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform that lived during the Late Cretaceous in Tajikistan.
facts.quote: Tadzhikosuchus (also spelt Tajikosuchus) is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous of Tajikistan.

facts.statement: The type species Tadzhikosuchus macrodentis was described by Efimov in 1982 from fossils found in the Ialovachsk Formation of the Fergana Basin in Tajikistan.
facts.quote: the type species T. macrodentis, described by Efimov in 1982 from the lower Santonian-age Upper Cretaceous Ialovachsk Formation of Kansai, Tajikistan, in the Fergana Basin of Tajikistan

facts.statement: A second species, Tadzhikosuchus neutralis, was named by Efimov in 1988 from the same location as the type species.
facts.quote: T. neutralis from the same location, by Efimov in 1988

facts.statement: A third species, Tadzhikosuchus kizylkumensis, was described by Nesov and colleagues in 1989 from Turonian-age rocks in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: T. kizylkumensis from Turonian-age rocks of the Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation of Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan, by Nesov and colleagues in 1989

facts.statement: A 2000 review by Storrs and Efimov suggested that the three named species could not be differentiated and should all be grouped under T. macrodentis.
facts.quote: a 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov could not differentiate between the species based on their type material, and recommended grouping the specimens of all three species under T. macrodentis

facts.statement: Researchers could not determine the relationship between Tadzhikosuchus and Zhyrasuchus, or if they were synonyms, because the available fossils were poor.
facts.quote: They also could not determine how Tadzhikosuchus and the contemporaneous Zhyrasuchus were related, or even if they were synonyms, due to the poor fossils available

facts.statement: Tadzhikosuchus is currently known primarily from partial lower jaws (dentaries).
facts.quote: To date, Tadzhikosuchus is mostly known from partial dentaries

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database classifies Tadzhikosuchus within the parent group Crocodylinae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the family of Tadzhikosuchus as Crocodylidae.
Tadzhikosuchus lived between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Martin and Delfino suggested in 2010 that Tadzhikosuchus likely belonged to the family Paralligatoridae rather than being similar to Prodiplocynodon.
rejected.quote: They instead suggested that it may have belonged to the Paralligatoridae, which was common in Asia at the time
